label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
**★☆☆☆☆ Good software, no support when it counts**

**Bridger Bend Community Library, Bozeman, MT**

We're a one-branch library with two full-time staff, a handful of volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. In June 2026 we signed a three-year contract with Stackhouse Cloud at $14,200 a year to move our catalog and circulation. We went live on October 19.

The good part first. The demo was impressive, and the staff interface is better than our old system. I still believe in what Stackhouse is trying to build. My complaint is with support.

Since October 28, checkouts have only worked in offline mode on a single laptop. The same failure wiped our holds queue, about 640 holds gone. Our support ticket has been open for 12 days. We've had three replies, and every one said the issue had been "escalated to engineering." Nothing after that.

During the sales process we were promised a dedicated migration specialist. What we got was a shared inbox.

This has real consequences for us. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes to pick up the large-print Westerns he had on hold. We had no record of the hold and had to send him home empty-handed. One of our volunteers is writing checkouts on index cards. Our line item is on the agenda at the county budget hearing on November 18, and right now I can't tell our commissioners when the system we're paying for will work.

**To Stackhouse leadership:** I'm asking for a named person with authority to call me this week. I don't need another ticket update. I need someone who can tell me what broke, who is fixing it, and when.

**To other library directors, especially at small libraries:** Before you sign, get support response times and escalation commitments in writing. If the sales rep promises a dedicated specialist, make sure the contract says so. A good product is only as good as the help you get when it fails, and small libraries don't have an IT department to fall back on.

I'm giving one star for now. If Stackhouse fixes this and stands behind its promises, I'll come back and update this review. I'd be glad to.

*Director, Bridger Bend Community Library*
